engagement_title: Argent & Faith spring capsule: bring a two-morning bench shoot to one house look, recover the maker's mark out of the engraved bench block, and carry both onto the product pages, the boxed provenance cards and the stockist lookbook
vertical: Jewelry, Watches & Accessories (independent silver studio, Providence, Rhode Island, direct plus eleven independent stockists)
real_brief_anchor: Primary anchor: the Freelancer.com silver-jewellery lead behind the ledger entry for this slot, a seller wanting a 'modern design for a rosary necklace', silver as the primary material, a clean modern aesthetic and 'good communication skills for revisions'. The posted ask is to design and model a piece from scratch, which the connector grades out of scope (no text-to-image, no 3D, no from-scratch art), so the ledger honestly re-cast it as the production-art package such a seller commissions around supplied bench captures. Co-anchor: the Upwork jewellery/accessory brief that took a signature bracelet from concept through manufacturing for a new lifestyle brand, whose in-scope slice is the launch-imaging workload once prototypes exist, scaled from one hero to a whole opening capsule so cross-asset consistency is actually present. Co-anchor: the Freelancer.com silver-jewellery photo-editing open call asking for handheld product frames turned into a clean, colour-accurate, uniform set with 'pure/near-white background with no colour cast', 'accurate metal tone and true gemstone colour', plus 'matching transparent cut-outs for layering, delivered store-ready'. The ledger records that the last of those was amputated to one hero and called a repeatable recipe, which deleted the only genuinely hard thing in it. PHOTO-13 restores the full commission those three clients actually had: a ten-piece capsule shot over two mornings, a mark that exists only as an engraving, a boxed card the printer holds and the studio does not, and a stockist lookbook that has to stay editable. Brands are laundered to the fictional Argent & Faith; no real house, person or trademark appears.
client_one_liner: Ten pieces, five weeks, and the stockist order window opens the same day the pages go live, so the photography, the mark, the boxed cards and the lookbook all have to come back from one person looking like one studio.
client_brief:
Argent & Faith, spring capsule: product pages, boxed cards and the stockist lookbook.

We are a two-bench silver studio in Providence. Nora cuts and pierces, I finish and set, and we put out ten pieces a season, sold direct and through eleven independent stockists. The capsule goes live in five weeks and the stockist order window opens the same day, so all of it has to come from one person and look like one house.

The photography is where we are stuck. A friend shot the capsule for us on the bench under the north window, then came back a second morning for the three pieces that were still at the polisher. Every frame is good on its own. Put them in a row on a product page and they do not look like the same studio made them.

First we need the pieces themselves, cleanly separated from whatever is behind them and sitting on a plain ground, ready to drop into a listing. Two things matter more than anything else. The open centres of the bands and the pierced work in the medallion have to be genuinely open, because the negative space is the design and a filled centre reads as a casting fault to anyone who knows silver. And a piece has to look like it belongs on the ground it is sitting on, not like it was lifted off one surface and dropped onto another.

We want our mark back too. It exists as an engraving in the steel bench block Nora's teacher cut for her, and nowhere else. We need it as artwork we can place at any size: on the pages, at the foot of the boxed cards, and reversed out of dark on the lookbook cover. It has to stay our mark, not a tidier mark that resembles it.

Then the printed side. Every piece ships in a box with a card carrying its name, its metal and finish, its dimensions, its provenance line and its number. Our printer has last year's file. We do not, and the woman who made it has retired. Keep the card as it is, change everything on it, and send back a press file plus one card per piece, named so we can pull the right one without opening it.

Last, the stockist lookbook: a cover, a spread of the range and two social canvases, all in one working file we can edit ourselves, plus whatever it was built from. We will be changing prices and we are not paying for a redo every season.

On tone: pieces run one hundred eighty to nine hundred dollars and our buyer is twenty-eight to fifty-five, buying one considered thing rather than three cheap ones. Quiet, plenty of air, the metal doing the work. And if anything in our own list looks wrong to you, tell us.
price_band_and_audience: Retail 180 to 900 dollars (open bands 180 to 260, pierced medallion 420, signet 560, reliquary locket 900). Buyer 28 to 55, Northeast urban and coastal, buys one considered piece for herself or as a milestone gift and reads the metal and dimensions before buying. The band is load-bearing. At this tier the listing tile is mostly ground, the piece sits small and centred, the type is quiet and the provenance line is treated as editorial copy. A filled ring centre or a piece that reads as pasted onto its ground is not a cosmetic flaw here, it reads as a casting fault or a faked photograph and it kills the sale. If the same capsule sold at 25 dollars the correct answer would be the opposite artefact: busy flat-lays, four pieces to a tile, a price flash, and nobody would look at the centre of a band. An agent that ships a dense, price-led, high-saturation set has misread the commission even if every technical gate passes. A real posted job of this shape runs 1,600 to 3,200 dollars fixed, or 50 to 80 dollars an hour for 30 to 45 hours.

brand_identity.tagline: Let the metal do the work.
brand_identity.sector: Independent silver jewellery studio: a two bench workshop putting out a ten piece capsule each season, sold direct and through eleven independent stockists.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2016, a two bench silver studio in Providence, Rhode Island, run by two makers.
brand_identity.about: Argent & Faith is a two bench silver studio. Nora cuts and pierces, her partner finishes and sets, and we put out ten considered pieces a season: open bands, a pierced medallion, a signet, a reliquary locket. We sell direct and through eleven independent shops. The negative space in a band or a piercing is the design, so how a piece is made and photographed matters as much as what it costs.
brand_identity.audience: Buyers aged 28 to 55, Northeast urban and coastal, buying one considered piece for themselves or as a milestone gift and reading the metal and dimensions before purchase.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Fine but accessible silver at 180 to 900 dollars a piece. Above high street silver, below designer gallery jewellery. At this tier the tile is mostly air, the piece sits small and centred, the type is quiet and provenance reads as editorial copy.
brand_identity.typography: Display in a refined high contrast serif with quiet authority; text in a clean neutral sans set small with air. The feel is considered and editorial, the metal leading and the type receding.
brand_identity.voice: Spare, precise, provenance led. We write in Nora's own plain words about how a piece was made. Example line the brand would write: 'Hand sawn and pierced, sterling silver, oxidised and hand finished at the bench.'
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: Our maker's mark exists only as an engraving in the steel bench block Nora's teacher cut for her, and nowhere else. There is no file and no one to ask, so the mark needs recovering from a photograph as artwork that stays true to the original rather than a tidier version of it.
brand_identity.values: Honest metal and honest making, and negative space treated as the design rather than a gap.

assets_supplied.name: bench_capsule/ (10 frames, 5472 x 3648)
assets_supplied.kind: Product photography shot by a friend of the studio across two mornings on the same light grey paper sweep on the finishing bench, one piece per frame.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The whole capsule, shot on the bench under the north window. Three of them were still at the polisher so he came back a second morning. They look fine one at a time."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two faults, neither stated. (1) The second morning was overcast and a warm work lamp was switched on over the bench, so the three catch-up frames (Quarry Band, Vesper Medallion, Crescent Studs) carry a different illuminant from the other seven. Each looks entirely plausible alone, which is why the client believes they match. (2) The four high-polish pieces are mirrors. The grey sweep and the softbox are reflected in their shanks and bezels as a broad cool band that is part of the metal, not part of the background. While the pieces sit on the sweep they were shot on, this is invisible and correct. The moment a cut-out piece is placed on any other ground, the reflected cool band stays in the silver and the piece reads as lifted off one surface and dropped onto another. No selection, knockout, crop or adjustment reports anything about it, every call returns success, and the failure is only visible with several isolated pieces laid on the chosen ground at listing size.

assets_supplied.name: bench_block_mark.jpg (4032 x 3024)
assets_supplied.kind: Hand-held phone photograph, shot square-on, of the studio's maker's mark engraved into the face of a polished steel bench block.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Our mark, cut into the bench block by Nora's teacher. It is the only version of it that exists. We never had a file and there is nobody to ask."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The mark is incised into polished metal rather than printed in ink, and the block was lit from the left. Every stroke therefore reads as a bright specular flank on one side and a dark shadow flank on the other, with the true stroke width lying between them. A selection that names the mark as a dark engraved line takes the shadow flank only, so a trace made from it comes back with every stroke at roughly half its true weight and displaced consistently to one side. At canvas size this looks crisp, deliberate and entirely correct. It only declares itself as the wrong mark at the size the card foot and the lookbook cover actually reproduce it, and against the dark ground where the thin side of each stroke drops out. The mark also carries a fine assay-style border ring with an enclosed interior and two small closed counters, and how much of that ring survives this photograph's engraving through a trace is an empirical property of this frame that no tool reports.

assets_supplied.name: provenance_card_2026_PRINT.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The printer's flat press PDF for last season's boxed provenance card, 105 x 74 mm landscape, one card per piece, font subsets embedded, produced from a real page layout so it converts cleanly.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "What the printer ran last year. We do not have the working file and the woman who made it has retired. Keep the card as it is."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two structural facts nobody at the studio could tell you and nothing in the PDF announces. (1) The mark printed at the foot of the card is not a placed graphic. Prepress flattened it into the card's background artwork, so the conversion exposes exactly ONE graphic frame, the piece photograph, and no frame anywhere that the recovered mark can be bound into. The client has asked for the mark at the foot of every card and there is no place to put it. (2) The piece name, the metal and finish line and the dimensions line came across as one continuous story rather than three addressable frames, so those three fields have to be driven by ordered character offsets inside a single story while the provenance line and the piece number sit alone.

assets_supplied.name: capsule_inventory.csv
assets_supplied.kind: Export from the studio's inventory system, one row per piece, with columns for piece name, metal and finish, dimensions, provenance line, piece number, retail price and a photo filename.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Ten pieces straight out of inventory. The provenance lines are Nora's own words and they go on the card as written."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two faults, neither stated. (1) The photo column points at a folder of web copies the studio made for its old site: 900 px JPEGs, already downscaled and already sharpened. Every filename resolves, every key binds, every card gets a photograph and nothing anywhere reports a problem. The cards simply print soft at trim, and no enlargement can put back what the studio's own export threw away, so the image map has to be rebuilt against the agent's own graded masters. (2) The provenance lines for the Vesper Medallion and the Lattice Pendant are swapped. The clerk copied one cell into the wrong row, so a pierced and hand-sawn medallion is described as cast solid and chased. Both rows are internally well formed, both bind, and only reading the copy against what the photograph actually shows settles it.

assets_supplied.name: house_notes.txt
assets_supplied.kind: Half a page of colour and tone language from Nora, with no hex values and no measurements.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "How we talk about the work: cold light, warm hand, oxidised recesses left dark, nothing bright, nothing bouncing."

assets_supplied.name: boxed_card_in_hand.jpg
assets_supplied.kind: Phone snap of last season's card sitting in its box, supplied as a feel reference.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "What the customer actually opens. This is the feeling we want kept."

acceptance_bar: Every listing image shows the piece cleanly separated from what was behind it, sitting on the plain ground we agreed, optically centred with nothing touching the edge.
Open centres are open and pierced work is pierced. A filled band centre or a closed piercing is a rejected file, not a note for later.
Every isolated piece must look like it belongs on the ground it is on, inspected with several pieces side by side at listing size, not one at a time.

The ten pieces read as ONE capsule when laid out in a row: one white point, one warmth in the metal, one black point, one crop logic. A frame that cannot be brought to the set is named to us, not shipped at eighty percent.

No file you hand back is larger than the frame it came from. Where reaching a size would have meant inventing pixels you chose a different crop, and the note lists every picture that was resized and by how much.

Our mark comes back as artwork we can scale and place on any ground, transparent, with nothing sitting behind it, and it still reads as our mark at the size it prints at the foot of the card and reversed out of dark on the cover.
In the lookbook file the mark is real vector artwork and the words are live text we can retype, not a picture of a page.

Boxed cards: exactly one page per piece, in inventory order, every line the old card carried present on every page, the photograph on each card the piece named on that card, at real print resolution at 105 x 74 mm trim.
One card file per piece, named so a jeweller can pull the right one without opening it, and its contents are what its name claims.
The lookbook comes back as one working file holding all four canvases at their own sizes, plus the self-contained source it was built from.
One type system across cover, spread and both social canvases, with the note naming per role the family, its foundry or designer, and the weight actually used.

A written note: what was done to each photograph, anything in our own list you questioned and what you did about it, and anything you could not do inside the card as it stands, told to us before it goes to the printer rather than after.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Photoshop and Lightroom imaging, including image_vectorize, counted here and not as an Illustrator surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload, asset_inline_preview, image_auto_straighten, image_apply_adjustments (masked and unmasked), image_select_by_prompt with returnBbox, image_select_subject, image_invert_selection, image_fill_area, image_remove_background (backgroundColor route only, on the pieces that are single coherent solids), image_crop_to_bounds, image_crop_and_resize with its tradeoffs array, image_vectorize
adobe_surfaces.role: Every raster and vector-recovery decision lives here. It brings two mornings of bench photography to one house neutral piece by piece rather than in one batched parameter set, routes the isolation per piece because a knockout cannot punch an enclosed band centre or a pierced tracery, derives the listing squares and the card-ratio masters at or below source scale, and recovers the mark out of an engraving in polished steel where the only lever on trace quality is the raster preparation, since the tracing call takes no options at all.

adobe_surfaces.surface: InDesign layout, merge-template authoring, data merge and print render
adobe_surfaces.tools: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml (twice: once to read the converted card, once to audit the prepared template), generate_indd_mapping_prompt as generator and as validator, prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout (application/x-indesign and application/pdf, additionalImageFiles, recordRange), document_render_layout (resolution 300, createSeparateFiles, pageRange in N-N form)
adobe_surfaces.role: The printed half. The printer's flat card becomes a live merge template with no working file to start from, the inventory export becomes the data source, and the run yields the press file, the per-piece named cards and the 300 ppi proofs. This is the only surface in the connector that does record per page, and it is the surface on which the client's request to have the mark at the foot of every card has to be answered.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Express, HTML authoring to a native editable document
adobe_surfaces.tools: get_account_type, create_visual_design_express_skill, html_export_readiness_skill, asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload with media_type text/html for the transport, export_html_to_express({url}), asset_search(CCAsset), asset_get_presigned_urls, asset_inline_preview
adobe_surfaces.role: The stockist lookbook: four roots at four canvas sizes in one export, cover and range spread plus a square and a tall social canvas, delivered as a native editable document with live text and the recovered mark as real vector shapes. This is the deliverable the merge surface structurally cannot give them, because a merge template does no free-form layout.

adobe_surfaces.tools: font_recommend once per typographic role, font_styles for the numeric OpenType weights, find_fonts to launder every name into canonical PostScript form, get_fontkit_embed_url for one kit consumed through the returned kebab css_stack
adobe_surfaces.role: The type system carried across cover, spread and both social canvases, and specified in the handover. The recommender refuses to pair by design, so the pairing is the agent's own art direction against a 180 to 900 dollar band and a considered buyer. Numeric weight is non-standard per family and cannot be inferred from a style name, a display cut is reached by its own slug, and one unresolvable name kills the whole kit including the valid faces beside it.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Stock plus Boards, counted as one surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_search(entityScope StockAsset, short generic queries, contentType filter, never orientation), asset_license_and_download_stock, boards_create_new_board, boards_add_items_to_board
adobe_surfaces.role: One licensed bench-atmosphere frame for the lookbook cover, which the studio cannot shoot before the deadline and which is the only IP-clean way to introduce a frame nobody at the studio took, plus the persistent selects board the two founders and their stockist rep sign off from before the press file is committed.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook before writing any markup, and settle which half of the commission lands on which surface.
trajectory.judgement: The split is the first real decision and the brief never states it. The boxed cards are record per page against a layout the client wants preserved, so they belong on the merge surface. The lookbook needs four canvas sizes and has to stay editable next season, so it belongs on HTML authoring. Reversing this either discards the card layout the client asked to keep or discovers that record per page cannot produce four different canvas sizes. The brief also pins the delivery destination, so there is nothing here to stall on.
trajectory.produces: A written plan naming surface per deliverable, and the confirmed account tier that gates the export at the end.

trajectory.action: Upload every supplied asset through initialize, PUT and finalize, holding each presigned URL against its role.
trajectory.judgement: Ordinary handoff discipline, but the manifest is what keeps forty later artefacts straight.
trajectory.produces: A manifest of presigned URLs keyed by role.

trajectory.action: Preview all ten bench frames and triage: which morning each came from, which are level, how tight each piece sits in frame, how polished each surface is, and whether the piece in each frame is the piece the inventory row claims.
trajectory.judgement: The client asserts one shoot, and the agent has to look and disagree. It also has to read the copy against the pictures: a provenance line describing cast and chased work sitting on a sawn and pierced medallion is only catchable by looking. Taking the filenames and the copy on trust is the fast answer and it is not the same thing as looking.
trajectory.produces: A per-frame triage note covering session, level, tightness, surface finish and subject identity.

trajectory.action: Level the frames that are off level.
trajectory.judgement: Straightening reframes the subject and eats edge pixels, so it has to happen before any crop policy is fixed.
trajectory.produces: Levelled masters where needed, originals untouched elsewhere.

trajectory.action: Fix one house neutral from the best-lit frame and correct each piece toward it with its own parameter set.
trajectory.judgement: The target is a capsule, not ten good photographs. Three frames need a materially different correction to arrive at the same place, and one batched call would apply one identical parameter set to all ten. The agent has to hold one destination rather than optimising each frame alone, and record what it dialled per frame.
trajectory.produces: Ten graded masters at source scale with a per-frame parameter log.

trajectory.action: Masked corrections where a whole-frame grade is wrong: the oxidised recesses, the set stones, the brushed versus mirror faces on the same piece.
trajectory.judgement: Prompt wording is the whole gate. Naming the substrate pulls the selection to the sweep, naming the material's own visual properties pulls it to the metal. A mask that fringes has to be recognised as fringing rather than accepted because the call returned success, and selection edges come back hard rather than feathered.
trajectory.produces: Corrected frames where a global grade would have flattened the oxidised work or turned the stones grey.

trajectory.action: Recover the mark from the bench block: an ink-level selection naming the engraved line's own visual properties, correct polarity, a crop to the selection's own bounds, a trace, then give the trace a viewBox and remove the opaque full-canvas path that rides along underneath it. Build the on-light and on-dark colourways.
trajectory.judgement: Three decisions the tools do not make: how to word the selection so it takes the engraving and not the block, which polarity to trace, and whether to deliver the two-colour trace or the colour-accurate plate. The hygiene is invisible until the mark is placed on a coloured ground, and background removal is the wrong instrument entirely on a mark with an enclosed border ring.
trajectory.produces: A placeable, scalable, transparent mark with two colourways, and a note of the selection wording used.

trajectory.action: Propose two plain grounds for the listing images, a paper white and a warm ivory that flatters silver, and pick one against the price band and the buyer.
trajectory.judgement: Genuine taste work with a defence attached. A non-designer picks the ivory because it looks richer in the swatch. Whether it is the right answer for THIS capsule is not settled by the swatch.
trajectory.produces: Two proposed grounds and a written pick with its reasoning.

trajectory.action: Isolate every piece and route each one by what it actually is: the single coherent solids through the one-call knockout onto the chosen ground, the open bands and the pierced medallion and lattice through a material-named selection, inverted and filled to the ground so the negative space stays negative.
trajectory.judgement: A knockout cannot punch an enclosed hole. It returns a solid disc with the captured sweep still inside it, and it reports success. Which pieces need which route is a per-piece decision the agent makes by looking at the piece, not a policy it applies to the set.
trajectory.produces: Ten isolated pieces, each with the isolation route recorded.

trajectory.action: Lay the whole isolated capsule on the chosen ground at listing size, side by side, as a product page row would show it, and look.
trajectory.judgement: Judging the set as a set at the only moment the comparison exists. Ten pieces that each passed inspection alone are not the same thing as a page that holds.
trajectory.produces: A contact set of the capsule on the chosen ground, inspected as a row.

trajectory.action: Derive the listing squares and the card-ratio masters from the graded set, reading the confidence and tradeoff metadata each crop returns rather than trusting success.
trajectory.judgement: The tradeoff array is the only signal that a crop clipped, that a detection was weak, or that an output was interpolated upward toward the cap, and it is easy to skip. Small pieces in a large frame make the detection weakest exactly where the crop matters most.
trajectory.produces: Listing squares and card-ratio masters, with a no-enlargement record drawn from what each call reported.

trajectory.surface: Data preparation and Creative Cloud storage
trajectory.action: Reconcile the inventory export against the pictures and the founders' note, normalise it into a merge-shaped data file with an image column holding bare filenames under the prefix the merge contract requires, upload the graded card masters and build the image map against them.
trajectory.judgement: Real reconciliation. The photo column the client supplied does not point where the agent needs it to point, and the agent has to decide whether repointing a client's own data silently is the same act as repointing it and saying so. The client asked to be told.
trajectory.produces: The merge data file, uploaded card masters, the image map, and a first list of questions for the handover.

trajectory.action: Convert the card PDF to a native document, export IDML from it, unzip it, and read what actually came across: how many text frames, how many graphic frames, which object styles, the real integer page-item ids, and the true story text reconstructed by concatenating the content runs.
trajectory.judgement: The mapping strategy is decided here and the answer is a property of the client's PDF, not of the plan. The agent must also confirm there is a real addressable frame for everything it has promised to place, since the whole per-row image binding depends on there being a frame to bind to.
trajectory.produces: The converted document, its IDML, a frame inventory with real ids and bounds, and the reconstructed story text.

trajectory.action: Author the mapping against what the conversion exposed, validate it, prepare the merge template, then export IDML from the RESULT, unzip it and grep the story for every placeholder the mapping claimed to create.
trajectory.judgement: Not accepting a success message as evidence. Nothing in the chain instructs this verification and nothing warns if it is skipped. It is the only place the mapping's real yield is visible before pages exist.
trajectory.produces: A merge template whose placeholder inventory has been independently confirmed.

trajectory.action: Merge to a native document with the per-row images bound, render the press file and the proofs at 300 ppi, then produce the per-piece single-page files and name each to its piece, verifying identity by opening each file rather than by its position in the returned list.
trajectory.judgement: Route matters and it is irreversible in practice: merging straight to raster silently drops to screen resolution whatever resolution is asked for, and merging straight to PDF forfeits the per-record branch. Naming ten files by the order they came back is the fast wrong answer, and it is the failure a jeweller pulling a card from a box discovers.
trajectory.produces: The press card file, 300 ppi proofs, and ten identity-verified named single-page cards.

trajectory.action: Search with short generic queries for the bench-atmosphere frame the studio agreed to pay for, filter to photography, exclude generative-tech results, license and download at full resolution, then grade it toward the house neutral and lay it beside the capsule.
trajectory.judgement: Choosing a frame whose existing light can be brought to the house neutral rather than the prettiest thumbnail. A warm bench frame and a cold one are equally attractive at 240 px and only one will ever sit with the ten.
trajectory.produces: One licensed camera-scale frame, graded, judged in or out with the reasoning recorded.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per typographic role, pull the family style inventories to learn the real numeric weights, launder every name into canonical form, and build one kit for the whole system.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is entirely the agent's and has to answer to a quiet, considered band. The numeric weight cannot be inferred from the style name, a display cut is reached by its own slug rather than a heavy weight, and the CSS must use the returned kebab stack. Getting any of the three wrong ships the wrong face with no warning anywhere.
trajectory.produces: One kit, with family, foundry or designer and the actual numeric weight recorded per role.

trajectory.action: Author one self-contained HTML with four roots at four canvas sizes, base64-inline every photograph, place the mark as inline vector inside an explicitly sized and top-left anchored wrapper, declare family and weight on every text element, let each root carry its own canvas size, upload the HTML by the allowed-host route, run the readiness check and export. Then verify through the two channels that exist: resolve the document's rendition and look at canvas one, and parse the returned per-canvas markup for the other three.
trajectory.judgement: A photograph left as a URL is not a photograph, weight is not inherited from markup semantics, and a global canvas override collapses a mixed-size set. Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning, and the preview only ever shows the first canvas, so looking at canvas one is not looking at the deliverable.
trajectory.produces: A native editable Express document holding all four canvases, its durable source HTML, and a per-canvas markup audit.

trajectory.action: Create the selects board and add the graded capsule and the licensed frame within the per-call placement cap, treating a partial success as partial and re-sending only the entries named as failed. Then write the handover.
trajectory.judgement: What to escalate versus what to fix silently. The note has to be specific enough that the next freelancer can rebuild the card from the same PDF without repeating the archaeology, and honest enough that anything that could not be delivered inside the client's own card is named before the file reaches a printer.
trajectory.produces: A persistent shareable selects board with nothing silently dropped, and the written handover the acceptance bar requires.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the isolated pieces actually belong on the ground that was chosen for them. Four of the ten are high-polish, and the grey sweep and the softbox are reflected in their shanks and bezels as part of the metal. On the sweep this is invisible and correct. Once the pieces are cut out and laid on the warm ivory ground at listing size, those four carry a broad cool band that belongs to a surface that is no longer in the picture, and they read as lifted off one ground and dropped onto another while the six matte and brushed pieces sit perfectly. Nothing reports it: the selections are clean, the knockouts return success, the fills return success, and each piece inspected alone looks entirely finished.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot dodge it and care cannot either. The reflection is not a background to be removed, it is the subject's own surface, so no selection wording, polarity or route avoids it. It cannot be seen before the pieces are cut out, because on their original ground the reflection is the correct reflection. And it cannot be predicted from the frames, because how much of the sweep a given piece mirrors is a function of that piece's curvature and polish. (b) Nothing states it. The brief says a piece must look like it belongs on the ground it is sitting on, which is the client's own standing quality requirement of the same kind as any 'no sloppy masking' clause, and it says nothing about reflections, polish or which ground is at risk. The ground choice at step 8 is presented as an open taste decision with no hint that one option is materially harder than the other. (c) It is not a propagation re-run. The response is a design decision that invalidates an earlier one: either the ground pick changes (which changes the listing set, the card masters and the lookbook's ground), or four pieces need masked work confined to the reflected band on the metal itself, which is different work from anything done so far, or those four are re-shot and the client is told. The isolation is not simply re-fed with a different parameter.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Lay the isolated set on both candidate grounds and look at the polished pieces specifically. Then either re-take the ground decision from step 8 toward the neutral that the reflections can live on and re-derive the isolated set and the card masters against it, or go back into the imaging chain and run masked corrections on the reflected band on the four polished pieces before re-isolating them, checking the result adjacent rather than alone. Whichever route is taken, the lookbook's ground and the boxed card's photo treatment inherit it, so both have to be settled before the merge masters are uploaded.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A product page where four of the ten pieces visibly float on a ground they were never photographed on, on a capsule where the whole proposition is that the metal is honest and the photograph is not faked, in front of a buyer paying nine hundred dollars for a locket.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the printer's card actually exposes as editable structure. Two facts arrive only by converting and looking, and neither is under anybody's control: how the three copy lines came across (as three addressable frames or as one continuous story that has to be driven by ordered offsets), and whether every element the client asked for has a frame to live in. On this card the mark at the foot was flattened into the background artwork by prepress, so the conversion exposes exactly one graphic frame, the piece photograph, and there is no frame anywhere that the recovered mark can be bound into. The card renders perfectly without it and every tool in the chain reports success.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot avoid it. Frame granularity and what prepress flattened are properties of a document made by a retired designer and a printer nobody can ask. They are not parameters, they are not reported before the conversion, and there is no read-ahead. The trajectory reaches the answer by converting, exporting and reading, which is the only route there is. (b) Nothing states it. The brief says the mark should sit at the foot of the cards and that the card layout should be kept as it is. That is the client's requirement, not a description of the template's internals, and the brief mentions no frames, fields or offsets. The acceptance bar names an output requirement, that every line the old card carried is present on every page, which is the client's standing quality line rather than a warning. (c) It is not a propagation re-run. The mapping strategy itself changes shape (offset arithmetic inside one story rather than per-frame replacement), and the mark requirement has to be re-planned rather than re-run: it cannot be bound per record, so the agent must decide between accepting the flattened mark already printed on the card and saying so, rebuilding the card family on the authoring surface at the cost of the layout the client asked to keep, or telling the client the request cannot be met inside their own artwork. That is a different deliverable route, not the same operation on changed input.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Rebuild the mapping as ordered offsets computed from the reconstructed story rather than per-frame replacement, re-order any rows sharing a uid against the original text, re-validate, re-prepare, and re-verify by round-tripping the IDML and grepping for every placeholder before any page is merged. Then take the mark decision explicitly, carry it into the press file and the per-piece cards consistently, and write it into the handover as something the client is told before the printer sees the file rather than after.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A press run of boxed cards that binds name, dimensions and number correctly on every card while the metal and finish line is silently absent, and where the studio's mark, the one thing the client said had to be at the foot of every card, is quietly whatever the retired designer left baked into the artwork. Every tool in the chain reported success.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the recovered mark survives being made and being imported. The mark is an engraving in polished steel lit from one side, so every stroke has a bright flank and a dark flank with the true width between them, and a trace taken from the dark flank comes back at roughly half weight and displaced to one side. At canvas size that trace is crisp and looks correct. Only at the size the card foot and the cover actually reproduce it, and only against the dark ground the cover uses, does it show as a hairline ghost with its border ring broken. Separately, how the importer normalises the trace once it arrives (loose ungrouped geometry rather than one coherent mark) is reported by nothing except the returned markup, and the rendition preview shows canvas one only, so the answer for the other three canvases has to come from the markup rather than from looking.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot dodge it. Which flank a selection takes and how much of the border ring survives are functions of this photograph's lighting and this engraving's depth, and the tracing call takes no options at all, so the only lever is the raster preparation and the only way to learn which preparation is needed is to see the failure. There is no first-time-right to aim at, only an empirical answer at real size on the real ground. (b) Nothing states it. The brief asks for the mark back as artwork usable at any size, including reversed out of dark, and never mentions strokes, weights, flanks or minimum sizes. It does not ask how small the mark can safely go, which would have made this a stated deliverable. (c) It is not a propagation re-run. The response is to produce a different asset: re-select on the specular flank or across both flanks, trace the colour-accurate plate instead, or re-cast the cover lockup with the mark larger or demoted. The earlier deliverable changes, and the lookbook composition is re-authored around whichever decision that is.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-run the recovery with a selection worded for a different part of the incision or through the colour-accurate plate route, place the result at true card-foot size and at cover size on the dark ground and look at it there rather than at canvas size, re-take the cover lockup decision if the mark will not hold, re-author and re-upload the HTML, re-run the readiness check, re-export and verify again through both channels rather than assuming the second export took. The card foot decision from the earlier checkpoint has to be revisited with whatever mark actually survives.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A stockist lookbook whose cover carries a broken hairline ghost of the studio's mark on a dark ground chosen for a mark that no longer reads, and product pages carrying the same half-weight artwork at every size, delivered as the client's recovered logo with the export having reported success.

deliverables.name: Argent & Faith spring capsule photography
deliverables.spec: Ten client frames brought to one house neutral (one white point, one warmth in the metal, one black point, one crop logic) plus one licensed camera-scale frame graded into the same set, delivered as listing squares and card-ratio masters, every output at or below its source pixel dimensions, with a per-frame log of the corrections applied and of every resize any tool reported. One set with one look, not ten separately optimised photographs and not the same picture at several sizes.

deliverables.name: Isolated capsule on the plain ground
deliverables.spec: Ten pieces isolated from their sweep and delivered on the agreed plain ground, with genuinely open band centres and genuinely pierced tracery reading open ON THAT GROUND (the enclosed negative space filled to the delivered ground, because the connector cannot punch an enclosed alpha hole), plus transparent (alpha) versions for layering of the pieces that are single coherent solids. The isolation route is recorded per piece, because the pieces that are single coherent solids and the pieces that enclose negative space cannot be produced the same way: the coherent solids knock out to true transparency, while the open bands and the pierced medallion are filled to the agreed ground so the centre reads open rather than as a casting-fault plug. Each piece must hold when inspected adjacent to the others at listing size, on the ground it ships on.

deliverables.name: Recovered Argent & Faith maker's mark
deliverables.spec: The mark recovered from an engraving in the bench block as placeable, scalable vector geometry with a real viewBox and no opaque ground path riding along underneath it, in an on-light and an on-dark colourway, holding its stroke weight and its border ring at the size it reproduces at the foot of the boxed card and at cover size reversed out of dark. Accompanied by a short usage note covering the sizes and grounds it was verified on.

deliverables.name: Boxed provenance cards, press file plus per-piece named cards
deliverables.spec: 105 x 74 mm landscape, one piece per card in inventory order, page count equal to piece count, rendered at 300 ppi at trim. Every card binds name, metal and finish, dimensions, provenance line and piece number verbatim from inventory, plus that piece's own photograph. Accompanied by one single-page file per piece, named to the piece and identity-verified by opening it, and by 300 ppi proofs. Produced by reverse-engineering the printer's flat PDF into a live merge template, which is itself handed back with a record of how it was derived.

deliverables.name: Stockist lookbook as one editable document plus its source
deliverables.spec: A single native editable Express document holding four roots at four canvas sizes: cover, range spread, a square social canvas and a tall one. Live editable text throughout in one licensed type system, the mark as real vector shapes, every photograph carried as embedded image data rather than a reference. Delivered with the self-contained source it was authored from, which is the durable half: the studio edits the document next season and the source guarantees the design survives regardless of that document's own retention.

deliverables.name: Handover note and selects board
deliverables.spec: A written note recording per photograph what was applied, the type system by role with family, foundry or designer and the actual numeric weight, what the card conversion exposed and the mapping decisions taken against it, every inventory row questioned and how it was resolved, anything that could not be delivered inside the client's own card, and every resize any tool reported. Paired with a persistent shareable selects board carrying the graded capsule and the licensed frame with nothing silently dropped.

Check every crop_and_resize response's metadata.tradeoffs array for an upscale entry (crop_and_resize interpolates to a hard 2x cap and signals it only there) and every remove_background response for a downscaled tradeoff; require each resize to be transcribed in the handover.

Parse each canvas's returned markup for the importer's placeholder image data (reject any) and for any element whose resolved position exceeds its declared canvas width.

verifiers_auto.text: Exactly ten per-piece card files exist, each named to a piece, each containing the piece its name claims.
verifiers_auto.how: Confirm exactly 10 single-page files. Read the piece_name / piece_number off the content of each file and confirm it matches the piece asserted by its filename (e.g. the file named for AF-SP26-005 / Reliquary Locket must contain the Reliquary Locket card); reject any check that relies on the order the files were returned in, since multi-record raster order is documented as reversed.

verifiers_auto.text: The selects board exists and carries the full graded set plus the licensed frame with no unre-sent failures.

verifiers_auto.text: On every piece that encloses genuine negative space, the delivered on-ground listing image carries the exact agreed ground colour inside the enclosed interior, not the captured grey sweep. This applies to the four open bands (Quarry Band, Cloister Band, Vigil Band, Meridian Band) and the hand-pierced Vesper Medallion; it does NOT apply to the Lattice Pendant, which is closed cast relief with no holes.
verifiers_auto.how: For each of those five enclosed pieces, sample the pixels inside the enclosed interior region (the band centre, or the sawn piercings of the medallion) and require them to match the delivered ground hex within a tight tolerance (delta-E <= 3 against whichever ground was agreed at step 8: Paper White #F6F4EF or Warm Ivory Ground #EFE7D9), and require them NOT to match the captured light-grey paper sweep the pieces were shot on (about North Window Grey #B9BBB8). Do NOT test for alpha transparency through the enclosed interior: the connector cannot punch an enclosed alpha hole (remove_background clears only the outer background and fill_area is solid-fill only), so the connector-correct, gradeable outcome is the interior filled to the delivered ground so the centre reads open. Reject any interior still carrying the captured sweep, and do not apply this check to the Lattice Pendant.

verifiers_human.text: Laid out as a product page row, the ten pieces read as one capsule rather than ten good photographs.
verifiers_human.how: View the delivered listing set side by side at listing size and judge white point, metal warmth, black point and subject scale as a set.

Do not expect alpha transparency through an enclosed band centre or piercing; that interior is delivered filled to the agreed ground, which is the connector-correct result.

verifiers_human.how: Compare the delivered mark at both reproduction sizes against the bench block photograph, looking for half-weight strokes and a broken ring.

verifiers_human.text: The design answers the 180 to 900 dollar band: air, quiet type, the metal doing the work, prices set plainly rather than flashed.
verifiers_human.how: Review the lookbook canvases and listing set against the price band and buyer description, and reject a dense, high-saturation, price-led answer.

verifiers_human.text: The handover escalates rather than conceals: the questioned inventory rows and anything that could not be done inside the client's own card are named in writing.
verifiers_human.how: Read the handover note against the triage findings and the conversion findings and check that each is disclosed with the decision taken.

decision_gates: The surface split: boxed cards to the merge surface because they are record per page against a layout the client wants preserved, lookbook to HTML authoring because it needs four canvas sizes and has to stay editable.
Whether the ten frames are one shoot. The client says they are and three of them are not.
Which ground the capsule ships on, decided as a taste question at first and then re-decided against what the polished pieces actually do on it.
Isolation route per piece: the one-call knockout is right for a coherent solid and wrong for anything enclosing negative space, and the wrong route returns a filled centre that reports success.
Whether the inventory copy matches the pictures, when two provenance lines are internally well formed and simply attached to the wrong pieces.

Whether to bind the client's own web-copy photo references or rebuild the image map against the agent's graded masters, and whether repointing a client's data silently is the same act as repointing it and saying so.
Whether to trust the mapping readout of the client's text or to reconstruct the story independently from the document.
Whether a success message counts as verification, when nothing instructs a re-export and grep of the prepared template and nothing warns if it is skipped.
How to answer a request that the client's own artwork cannot carry, once it is clear there is no frame for the mark on the card.
Whether to name ten per-piece card files by the order they came back or by opening each one.
Selection wording on the engraving: which flank of an incised line the prompt takes, and whether the resulting trace is the mark or a ghost of it.
Which mark variant carries the cover, judged at reproduction size on the dark ground rather than at canvas size.

The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged against a considered buyer and a 180 to 900 dollar band, and the real numeric weight per family, which cannot be inferred from a style name.
Whether the licensed bench frame joins the capsule or reads as bought, and if it reads as bought, whether to push it or search again on the light rather than the subject.
why_not_vlm: Paste this brief and these assets into a frontier image model and it returns pictures of jewellery. It fails all three gates. IDENTITY: these are ten specific pieces a buyer receives in a box, and the mark is a specific engraving cut by a named teacher into a specific bench block. A regenerated ring is a different object being sold under a photograph of it, and a regenerated mark is another studio's logo. At 900 dollars for a locket that is not a stylistic shortfall, it is misrepresentation. SPEC: the client needs one card per piece in inventory order at 105 x 74 mm and 300 ppi with five named fields bound verbatim from their own system, ten separately named card files that each contain the piece their filename claims, listing images on an agreed ground with genuinely open centres, and no delivered file larger than its source. A generated image satisfies none of that and cannot be checked against an inventory export. EDITABILITY: two deliverables are defined by being editable, a live merge template so next season is a data change rather than a re-commission, and a native document with live text and real vector geometry so the studio changes prices itself. And the middle of the engagement is verification against material reality: does this placeholder exist, is the photograph on this card the piece named on it, does this cutout belong on this ground, does this trace hold its ring at card-foot size. None of that is a generation problem.
doability_proof: Every link is verified in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account), the surface count is five and honestly declared, and image_vectorize is counted in the Photoshop family rather than as an Illustrator surface. MERGE SPINE: building a merge template from a bare PDF end to end headlessly is verified (convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt, prepare_indd_merge_template producing a story containing the expected placeholders), one record per page is confirmed for PDF output, per-record named files are confirmed by two order-verified routes (createSeparateFiles and a recordRange loop) while multi-record raster order is documented as reversed and is therefore never used for identity, and true 300 ppi comes from document_render_layout because outputSpecs.resolution on the merge itself is documented as silently ignored. THE CARD PDF IS BUILT TO A VERIFIED SHAPE: v3 observed that a continuous flow with no placed images collapses to one text frame with zero graphic frames, while interleaved images split it into two text frames plus two graphic frames. This card places one photograph in its own block with three copy lines running contiguously beside it and the mark flattened into the background artwork, so the expected yield is one graphic frame plus a small number of text frames, with the three contiguous lines sharing one story. The PDF must be a real font-embedding press PDF produced by a full engine, since v3 records that a thin hand-authored PDF fails conversion opaquely. The flattened-mark fact is a property of the manufactured asset and is verify-then-ship: before admission, run the conversion and confirm the mapping inventory returns exactly one graphic frame. IMAGE BINDING: per-row image merge through an at-prefixed CSV column plus additionalImageFiles keyed to bare filenames is verified at three keys; this task binds ten, so the trajectory carries the verified recordRange loop as an explicit fallback, which also guarantees per-record identity. IMAGING: auto_straighten, apply_adjustments masked and unmasked, select_by_prompt with returnBbox, invert_selection, fill_area, crop_to_bounds, crop_and_resize with its tradeoffs array, remove_background with backgroundColor and vectorize are all verified headless across 27 live calls. The enclosed-aperture failure of remove_background is a verified live finding (a solid opaque disc where a true knockout would have been transparent), as are the substrate-versus-ink prompt asymmetry, the binary non-anti-aliased mask, vectorize's missing viewBox and opaque path zero, and the explosion into loose ungrouped shapes in Express. UPSCALING IS HANDLED NOT ASSERTED: crop_and_resize interpolates to a hard 2x cap and signals it only in metadata.tradeoffs, and remove_background silently downscales oversized inputs and reports it only as a downscaled tradeoff, so the acceptance bar scores the decision and the disclosure as separable clauses. EXPRESS: multi-root export with mixed canvas sizes in one document is verified, mm canvases resolve exactly at 96 dpi, inline SVG becomes native editable vector, and the product is a genuine editable document in Creative Cloud. Transport is pinned to the upload route with media_type text/html because inlined photography passes the readiness skill's 70 KB inline threshold, which v3 warns triggers a user-facing warning. Verification is split to match the two channels that exist, since the rendition preview shows page one only. Persistence is not assumed, so the deliverable is the Express document plus the durable source HTML. FONTS: font_recommend, font_styles, find_fonts, get_fontkit_embed_url is verified end to end including a real browser loading licensed faces, and the non-standard numeric weights, the slug-not-PostScript CSS rule and the all-or-nothing kit call are live findings the task leans on. STOCK AND BOARDS: short generic queries only (long queries return zero hits and the orientation filter is broken), asset_license_and_download_stock returns genuine camera-scale files, and boards placements are capped at twelve per call with partial success signalled by failedItems and SVG unsupported, all encoded in the trajectory and the bar. AVOIDED: no video or audio, no document_render_vector or document_merge_data_vector, no variable QR, no bleed requirement, no pdfPreset, no fill_text, no animate_design or create_firefly_board, no replace_image, no download_design, no upscaling, no OCR, no compositing, no generated imagery, no photo reaching Express as a URL, and no batch above twenty files.
